This will be a simple explanation of how I do this process of unwinding some like to call meditation. Other guides will tell you differently probably, but the way I do it is very similar to the /r/meditation guidelines. It would most accurately be labeled mindfulness if you must label it.

Sit in meditation at least 40 minutes every day. Unless you're busy. Then sit double that.

-- Some genius (botched quote)

  • Find a nice comfortable area in which to sit, lie or whatever. It should preferably be a cool, dry area. I'd recommend sitting with your back straight in a comfy chair. It can even be a recliner if you're lazy. If you sit on the floor, then put a rolled up towel or small cushion down to put your butt on. This helps keep straight posture. Very important.

  • Look at the clock (starting on an even number is nice) and close your eyes, noting the time. You will start out doing 10 minute sessions, twice a day. You need at least 20 minutes.

  • Close your eyes and breath in slowly through your nose and out your mouth. As I exhale I like to repeat a mantra like "om". It gives you something to focus on. You can also let yourself zone out to the sounds of the air coming in and out of your nostrils/mouth. It's soothing to breathe deeply. Oxygen is needed for us to not only survive, but to relax.

  • With that said, focus (or more accurately not focusing at all) your mind on a simple display which brings you peace. I personally imagine a giant waterfall washing away my anxieties. This grounds your thoughts as they keep trying to race back to "where did I leave my keys" or "did I pay my bills?". It is very important to learn to let these thoughts flow through your mind freely. Your mind should not be a sponge right now. It should be more like a mesh screen. Don't be upset that you can't banish all these "bad" thoughts. However, enable yourself to let them slip through your mind, like a gentle breeze.

  • Repeat the long, slow breaths, hum your mantra, keep your focus on the breathing and your peaceful place, and let those thoughts keep on slippin'. (into the future, future)

  • Open your eyes when you feel it's time. If you started your session at 9:30, then you're done at 9:40. This isn't very professional practice and you may need an alarm set in the beginning, but I feel it ruins the session anticipating it.

Congrats, you've just meditated. Feel better? Any calmer?
